messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: ordinal logistic regression
parts:
I think we should implement an ordinal logistic
distribution as a new discrete multivariate
distribution, but I'd like some advice on parameterization.

It will be more efficient, more numerically stable,
and less error prone than implementing it directly in
the models a la BUGS and Gelman and Hill (see below).

Here's the Gelman and Hill style model, which I want
to keep:

Data:
K > 2, number of outcomes
y[n] in 1:K, K-way ordinal outcomes
x[n] in R^M, M-dimensional predictors

Parameters:
C[2],...,C[K-1] positive ascending, cut points
beta in R^M, regression coefficients

The likelihood function is:

Pr[y[n]=1] = 1 - inv_logit(x[n]*beta)

Pr[y[n]=2] = inv_logit(x[n]*beta)
- inv_logit(x[n]*beta - C[2])

Pr[y[n]=k] = inv_logit(x[n]*beta - C[k-1])
- inv_logit(x[n]*beta - C[k])

Pr[y[n]=K] = inv_logit(x[n]*beta - C[K-1])

I think we should implement this directly given
k rather than populating a categorical distribution.

My question is, should we implement the single outcome
case as something like this:

ordinal_logistic(int y,
double lambda,
vector<double>& c);

where lambda would be set to x[n]*beta for a regression problem,
and c[0],...,c[K-3] is just C[2],...,C[K-1] re-indexed (that'd
still be c[1],...,c[K-2] in Stan for maximal confusion).

In the Stan modeling language, this would look like:

y[n] ~ ordinal_logistic(x[n]*beta,c);

An alternative would be to assume the regression basis:

ordinal_logistic(y,
vector<double> x,
vector<double> beta,
vector<double> c);

This would look like:

y[n] ~ ordinal_logistic(x[n],beta,c);

The alternative is to follow BUGS and JAGS and
code everything in the model.

vector<K> theta;
theta[1] = ...calc with x[n], beta, c...;
theta[2] = ...;
for (k in 3:(K-1))
theta[3] = ...;
theta[K] = ...;

y[n] ~ categorical(theta);

The problem with this is that it's very wasteful. We usually
know what the y[n] value is, so really only need to calcuate
theta[n].

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ordinal logistic regression
parts:
On 4/30/12 8:47 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> When we meet on Wed, I can tell you about my ideas for a weakly informative prior for this model. I don't think we ever wrote this up, actually...

Sounds good. I was asking you about that
ages ago.

Daniel and I were thinking you could use
a simplex for the cutpoints once you took
an overall scale kappa.

Then you can make the simplex distribution
multivariate logistic for some generality
or just a simple Dirichlet with alpha > 1
to keep the cut points distinct.

- Bob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ordinal logistic regression
parts: I can't remember the details right now, but I think I was thikning about putting independent priors on the coefficients and then putting fractional prior "observations" on the categories in order to keep the cutpoints separated in sparse data settings, e.g., if you have responses on a 1-10 scale and you don't happen to see any 8's.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ordinal logistic regression
parts: I think adjacent-categories logit model might also be an option. It is more directly related to binary logit model, so extending weakly informative prior to it should be fairly straight-forward.
